title: Middle school English: reading comprehension
description: Four lessons on context vocabulary, sequence, main idea and inference with short English passages; prompts bilingual, passages in English.
assumptions: Short graded English passages; answers justified by the text.
stage1goal: Build vocabulary and sequence from context.
vocab-context.title: Vocabulary from context
vocab-context.goal: Infer word meaning from surrounding English text.
vocab-context.reading: The result clause explains the word: “exhausted … so he sat and rested” means very tired.
vocab-context.worked.prompt: In “Tom was exhausted after the long run, so he sat down and rested.”, what does exhausted mean?
vocab-context.clue.prompt: “The room was chaotic: toys everywhere.” Chaotic means…
vocab-context.clue.a.label: messy
vocab-context.clue.b.label: quiet
vocab-context.independent.prompt: “She whispered, so nobody heard.” Whispered means…
vocab-context.independent.a.label: shouted
vocab-context.independent.b.label: spoke quietly
vocab-context.c1.prompt: “He was famished, so he ate three bowls.” Famished means…
vocab-context.c1.a.label: very hungry
vocab-context.c1.b.label: thirsty
sequence.title: Sequence the story
sequence.reading: First/then/finally mark order: planted → sprouted → flowered.
sequence.worked.prompt: In “First we planted the seed. Then it sprouted. Finally it flowered.”, which event is last?
sequence.order.f.label: flowered
sequence.order.p.label: planted
sequence.order.s.label: sprouted
sequence.transfer-order.prompt: Order: finally we ate / then we cooked / first we bought.
sequence.transfer-order.e.label: finally we ate
sequence.transfer-order.c.label: then we cooked
sequence.transfer-order.b.label: first we bought
sequence.c1.prompt: Which connector marks the last event?
sequence.c1.a.label: first
sequence.c1.b.label: finally
main-idea.title: Find the main idea
main-idea.goal: Distinguish main idea from details in English.
main-idea.reading: The main idea covers all sentences: “Bees are useful” covers pollinate/honey/feed.
main-idea.struggle: Without listing details, explain how to find the main idea of an English paragraph.
main-idea.worked.prompt: In “Bees pollinate flowers, make honey, and feed their young. Bees are useful insects.”, why is “Bees are useful” the main idea?
main-idea.main.prompt: Main idea of the bee paragraph?
main-idea.main.a.label: Bees are useful
main-idea.main.b.label: Bees make honey
main-idea.transfer-main.prompt: “Rain fills rivers, waters crops, cools air.” Main idea?
main-idea.transfer-main.a.label: Rain cools air
main-idea.transfer-main.b.label: Rain helps life
main-idea.c1.a.label: cover the whole paragraph
main-idea.c1.b.label: list every detail
inference.title: Infer the author’s intent
inference.goal: Infer tone and intent beyond the literal English.
inference.reading: Tone and detail choices reveal intent: quiet forest + axes = mourning loss.
inference.worked.prompt: In “The forest quieted; only axes echoed. The birds had gone.”, what does the author feel?
inference.intent.prompt: “Recycle: cans become bikes, paper becomes boxes.” Intent?
inference.intent.a.label: Encourage recycling
inference.intent.b.label: Warn against bikes
inference.transfer-intent.a.label: praise logging
inference.transfer-intent.b.label: mourn loss of forest
inference.c1.a.label: title only
inference.c1.b.label: tone and details
inference.c2.a.label: encourages
inference.c2.b.label: warns
